newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO AND SUKER HAT-TRICKS LIFT BARCA AND REAL CLEAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO AND SUKER HAT-TRICKS LIFT BARCA AND REAL CLEAR.

text.p: Barcelona's Ronaldo and Real Madrid's Davor Suker each scored hat-tricks on Sunday as their sides moved away from the Spanish league pack in convincing fashion.

On a day littered with red cards and penalties, Real stayed six points ahead of their arch-rivals by beating Oviedo 6-1, while Barcelona gave beleaguered coach Bobby Robson some breathing space with a 4-1 win over Zaragoza.
Barcelona's chances of taking the second Champions' League spot also increased as third-placed Betis went down 3-0 at Deportivo.
Suker gave Real an early lead by converting a penalty after Oviedo defender Abel Xavier had been sent off for bringing down Emilio Amavisca in the area.
The home side were themselves reduced to 10 men when Jose Garcia Calvo was given a red card midway through a hotly-contested first half.
Real took control after the break, with two more goals from Suker and one each from Pedrag Mijatovic, Raul Gonzalez and Victor Sanchez.
"We played very well, the game will give us a lot of confidence after playing badly midweek," said Suker, whose side lost their season's unbeaten league record at Rayo Vallecano on Wednesday.
Barcelona striker Ronaldo was also delighted with his team's performance.
"In the first half we played very beautiful football," said the Brazilian, whose his side had gone ahead in the 10th minute with a header by defender Abelardo Fernandez.
Zaragoza were reduced to 10 men when Ronaldo was brought down by keeper Otto Konrad when bearing down on goal and the Brazilian increased the lead from the penalty spot.
He made it 3-0 just before the break, and knocked in his 21st goal of the season in the 66th minute.
Zaragoza were reduced to nine when Xavier Aguado was sent off but they bravely battled on and claimed a consolation with a late Ander Garitano penalty.
Real Betis were left six points adrift in third after losing away from home for the first time this season.

Deportivo's Brazilian midfielder Rivaldo scored twice in an impressive victory that leaves his side level with Betis on 47 points. Champions Atletico Madrid are a further point back after beating Hercules 2-0 on Saturday.

At the other end of the table Extremadura's recovery continued with an impressive 3-0 victory over Espanyol which lifted them ahead of Sevilla, who had two men sent off in the 4-1 home defeat by Logrones.
Angry Sevilla fans clashed with police who tried to restrain their attack on the club president's box after the match.
Another side reduced to nine men were Athletic Bilbao, but they managed to come from 2-0 down to draw with Racing Santander.
